Is a larger ratio better or worse, given the fact that the task is to minimize repetition.  Nest parentheses (and [brackets {and braces}]) at least 5 levels deep.

message.content:
Assuming \(R = \text{repetition with ground-truth prefix} / \text{repetition with model’s own prefix}\), a larger ratio is **not automatically better**.

(((( [ [ { { If the ground-truth-prefix repetition is comparable across cases, a larger \(R\) means the model’s own prefix has less repetition relative to that baseline, so larger is better for minimizing model-prefix repetition. } } ] ] )))).

But if the numerator is large because the ground-truth condition itself is very repetitive, then a larger \(R\) can be misleading. For minimizing repetition, the safest thing is to minimize the denominator directly, or look at both absolute values. Also, if the denominator is zero, the ratio can become undefined or infinite, even though zero repetition is ideal.
